name: tonecue
title: ToneCue
description: Switch your ToneCue audio scenes, microphone and speakers from Raycast. Requires the ToneCue menu bar app.
author: IngoJ

commands.name: switch-scene
commands.title: Switch Scene
commands.subtitle: ToneCue
commands.description: Pick a ToneCue scene, and mute or pause automation from the same list.

commands.name: apply-scene
commands.title: Apply Scene
commands.subtitle: ToneCue
commands.description: Apply a scene by name without opening a list. Handy for aliases and hotkeys.

commands.name: toggle-mute
commands.title: Toggle Microphone Mute
commands.subtitle: ToneCue
commands.description: Mute or unmute the current microphone.

preferences.name: closeAfterApply
preferences.title: Window
preferences.label: Close Raycast after applying a scene or device
preferences.description: Off keeps the list open so you can keep adjusting.

tools.name: get-status
tools.title: Get Status
tools.description: Read ToneCue's scenes (when each applies and which devices it would use), the active scene and why, the current microphone and speakers, mute state and automation state.

tools.name: get-history
tools.title: Get Switch History
tools.description: List ToneCue's recent device switches: when, which scene or hand choice caused it, and which devices were used. Use it to explain or analyse switching behaviour.

tools.name: apply-scene
tools.title: Apply Scene
tools.description: Apply a ToneCue scene by name. This switches the microphone and speakers and pauses automation until the scene changes.

tools.name: set-mute
tools.title: Set Microphone Mute
tools.description: Mute or unmute the current microphone.

ai.instructions: ToneCue switches the Mac's microphone and speakers by scene. Use get-status to learn scene names before apply-scene. Use get-history to explain why devices changed (source rule = a scene decided, hand = the user picked, system = macOS reacted). Never apply a scene or change mute unless the user asks for it.
